To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GM‐CSF‐impregnated gauzes are effective in preventing or healing dermatitis in vulvar carcinoma patients during radiation.
GM‐CSF‐impregnated gauzes are effective in reducing the severity and healing time of radiation‐induced vulvar dermatitis and in shortening the interruption intervals of the radiotherapy.

(1) GM‐CSF gauze is effective in reducing radiation‐induced skin reactions, (2) it is effective in reducing the duration of radiation treatment interruption, (3) it is effective for pain reduction, (4) the effect on skin reactions is not related to body mass index and (5) the effect on pain is not related to age, body mass index, and the application of steroids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new method of preventing and healing radiation dermatitis in patients with vulvar carcinoma.
the use of GM‐CSFs as an adjuvant treatment to prevent or reduce radiation‐induced skin damage and to improve the quality of life of the patients.
the use of a novel, simple, inexpensive, and effective treatment of radiation dermatitis in patients with vulvar cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has shown that GM‐CSF is effective in reducing the severity of radiation dermatitis, but the effect of GM‐CSFs is limited by the body mass index.
this study shows a positive effect of GM‐CSf‐gauze on radiation induced dermatitis.
GM‐CSF gauze can reduce the radiation‐induced skin reaction in the treatment of vulvar carcinoma and can reduce the interruption of the radiotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GM‐CSF is an important factor in the treatment of radiation‐induced skin damage.

the application of GMCSF‐impregnated gauzes is effective in reducing the severity of the radiation‐induced dermato‐neuro‐sensory reactions in the irradiated areas and in reducing the interruptions in the radiotherapy course for the treatment of the vulvar cancer.
GM‐CSF‐impregnated gauzes can be an effective and safe method for preventing and healing radiation dermatitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of GM‐CSFs can be an effective tool in the management of radiation‐induced skin reactions.
the application of GMCSF impregnation gauze is an effective method in reducing radiation‐induced skin toxicity and pain in vulvar carcinomas.
GM‐CSF is an effective and safe treatment to prevent and heal radiation‐induced skin damage in patients with vulvar cancer.
